sections.title: The Wind
sections.passage: The wind was so strong that if you leant into it, it would hold you up. Jason was doing this when the wind suddenly died down. As his mother cleaned the graze on his knee, Jason told her what had happened. She laughed at the story.

responses.prompt: What happened to Jason when the wind died down?
Was Jason badly hurt? How do you know that?
responses.response: no because there was a graze on his knee

sections.title: Toast
sections.passage: Shane put the bread in the toaster, pushed the lever down and went on reading his book. Ten minutes later Tessa came into the kitchen. She looked at the toaster and flicked the switch on at the wall. It wasn't long before the toast was ready.

responses.prompt: Why didn't Shane notice that the toast wasn't cooking?
Why didn't the toast cook when Shane pushed the lever down?
responses.response: because the power point wasn't turned on

sections.title: Melissa
sections.passage:
Melissa looked back over her shoulder and saw the thick, dark clouds moving towards her. She heard the rustling leaves in the trees and pulled her new red hat down firmly on her head.

The bag on her bike was. still half full. Melissa pedalled as hard as she could, quickly pushing morning papers into mail boxes.

At last she was almost finished. She just had to cross the bridge then make the long ride up Riverside Street.

Her bag now empty, her legs tired and sore, Melissa turned her bike around. She freewheeled down Riverside Street towards home. The clouds were almost overhead but there was no rain yet, just wind. Melissa tried to grab her hat, but it had gone. She last saw it sailing over the side of the bridge. Then the rain came.

responses.prompt: Why did Melissa pull her hat down?
Why did she pedal as hard as she could?
responses.response: because her legs were tired and sore

responses.prompt: Where did Melissa's paper delivery finish?
responses.response: all of the papers were gone
there was a bridge you had to cross

responses.prompt: Why did Melissa's hat go sailing over the bridge?

questionScores.rationale: Incorrect. The passage implies a windy day, not 'middle of the day'.
Correctly inferred he was cooking bacon.
Correctly inferred he was cutting trees.
Correctly identified he only had a graze on his knee.
Correctly identified he was distracted by reading.
Correctly identified the switch at the wall was off.
Incorrect. She pedaled hard to finish before the storm hit, not because her legs were tired.
Incorrect. Answered 'all papers gone' instead of the location (near the bridge).
Incorrect. Riverside Street is described as a 'long ride up' and then 'freewheeled down', implying a hill.
